accepted.question_text: Which broad and mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds can be described explicitly? Here an affine Poisson manifold means a finite-dimensional manifold equipped with an affine atlas and a Poisson bi-vector P whose Schouten self-bracket [[P,P]] vanishes.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Describe ample classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds (M^r_aff, P).

accepted.question_text: Can one construct smooth-atlas globalisations of the known Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetries Q_{1:6/2}(P)=O→r(γ_3)(P), Q_5(P)=O→r(γ_5)(P), and Q_7(P)=O→r(γ_7)(P)? In this notation, O→r is the graph-orientation map that sends a graph cocycle γ to a universal infinitesimal symmetry Q(P) of Poisson bi-vectors.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Find the smooth-atlas globalisation(s) of the Kontsevich symmetries Q1: 6/2(P) = O→r(γ3)(P), Q5(P) = O→r(γ5)(P), and Q7(P) = O→r(γ7)(P), found in [2], [7], and [4] respectively.

accepted.question_text: For a graph cocycle γ=Σ_a c_a·γ_a on n vertices, are combinatorial statistics of the constituent graphs—such as diameter distributions and vertex-valency distributions—stable across the full cohomology class [γ]=[γ+d(λ)] after arbitrary coboundary changes by graphs λ on n−1 vertices? Relatedly, what is the large-n and asymptotic behavior of the dimension of graph cohomology, especially near the bi-grading ray (n, 2n−2) that is relevant for Poisson-bracket symmetries, and is there a generating function for those dimensions?
accepted.context_brief: Stability and asymptotics of graph cocycles

evidence.quote: Problem 3. As soon as the vertex number n is large enough, are the combinatorial properties of graphs γ_a in a cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a well defined, i.e. stable over the entire equivalence class [γ] = [γ + d(λ)] modulo arbitrary coboundaries from graphs λ on n − 1 vertices ? The properties to examine can be the distribution of diameters (over the set of graphs {γ_a} forming the cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a) and distribution of vertex valencies. • What is the large-n and asymptotic (n → ∞) behaviour of the graph cohomology dimension (primarily, on or near the ray of vertex-edge bi-gradings (n, 2n − 2), which is relevant to the Poisson bracket symmetries); are the dimensions encoded by their own generating function ?

accepted.question_text: How can Willwacher’s isomorphism grt ≃ H^0(Gra), between the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra and degree-zero cohomology of the relevant unoriented graph complex, be illustrated concretely at small vertex numbers such as n=4, 6, 8, 9, 10, ... where nontrivial cocycles already occur?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Illustrate the work of Willwacher’s isomorphism grt ≃ H0(Gra) at small vertex numbers n = 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, . . ., where there are nontrivial cocycles in Gra.

accepted.question_text: For the bi-grading ray (N, 2N), beginning at which N′>7 do nontrivial cocycles ω in the graph-complex kernel ker d exist, and beginning at which larger N′′ are those cocycles orientable to nonzero Kontsevich graphs built from wedges? Can one give explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P) using known cocycles γ and new cocycles ω on that ray?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Starting which N′ > 7, are there nontrivial cocycles ω ∈ ker d ? And starting which N′′ > N′, are these cocycles orientable (i.e. meeting no obstructions [9, App. A]) to nonzero Kontsevich’s graphs built from wedges ← •→? Give explicit examples of new symmetries P˙ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m≠0 · O→r(γ)(P) for known cocycles γ and new such ω on the ray (N, 2N).

accepted.question_text: For non-unique factorisations [[P,Q(P)]]=♦(P,[[P,P]]) of the Poisson-cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs, what is the topological structure of the resulting identities ♦₂−♦₁≡0? Equivalently, if one forms a meta-graph whose vertices are Leibniz graphs and where adjacency means that two Leibniz graphs have expansions sharing a Kontsevich oriented graph, what are the genus, diameter, typical cycle length, and related invariants of these meta-graphs, and how does the iterative generation algorithm saturate them?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Let us say that two Leibniz graphs are adjacent if their expansions have a Kontsevich orgraph in common. Now, describe the topological structure of the identities ♦2 − ♦1 ≡ 0 for known non-unique solutions of the factorisation problems. Otherwise speaking, describe the meta-graphs with Leibniz graphs as vertices: what is their genus, diameter, typical cycle length, etc. ? • Investigate the saturation curve for the number of Leibniz graphs produced by the iterative algorithm (e.g., see [9, Table 1]): at which stage are the new Leibniz graphs typically leaves vs handles ? What are the last new Leibniz graphs in this sense ?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist universal infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of Poisson structures that are nonlinear, proper, valid for all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds, and not produced from graph cocycles through Kontsevich’s orientation morphism O→r?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Are there any other nonlinear proper infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) ∈ sym([[P,P]] = 0) which are universal with respect to all (affine) Poisson manifolds of arbitrary finite dimension but which are not obtained from the graph cocycles by using Kontsevich’s orientation morphism O→r ?

accepted.question_text: If a graph cocycle γ generates the formal flow P(ε)=exp(ε O→r(γ)(P)·∂/∂P⃗)P|_{ε=0} on Poisson bi-vectors, does that graph-defined power series converge and determine a globally well-defined Poisson structure at every point of an arbitrary affine Poisson manifold?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Does the formal power series expansion P(ε) using graphs determine a globally well defined Poisson structure at all points of arbitrary affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P) ? In other words, do the power series converge (uniformly over M^r_aff) ?

accepted.question_text: What are the Liouville-integrability and possible super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems Ṗ = Q(P) that arise from known Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. What are the (Liouville, in particular super-)integrability properties of these nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems P˙ = Q(P) ?

accepted.question_text: Does the evolution equation Ṗ = Q(P) for Poisson structures itself carry a Poisson or Hamiltonian formulation on the jet space of Poisson bi-vector components, meaning that one can write Q(P)=π(χ(P)) for some variational Poisson structure π and variational covector χ, possibly χ=δH/δP for a well-defined Hamiltonian functional?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Does the evolution P˙ = Q(P) of Poisson structures P obey the above meta-principle implying that this evolution itself ought to be Poisson, Q(P) = π(χ(P)), where π is a variational Poisson structure on the jet space of Poisson bi-vector components and χ is a variational covector (possibly, the variational derivative δH/δP of a well defined Hamiltonian functional, cf. [16, 26]) ?

accepted.question_text: Consider the two-parameter family of Poisson brackets on R^3 defined by {f,g}_{a,ρ}(x,y,z)=ρ(x,y,z)·det(∂(a,f,g)/∂(x,y,z)), where a is a smooth function and ρ is a density in the chosen coordinates. Is this class preserved by any Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ=Q(P), and for a given symmetry does there exist an induced evolutionary system ȧ=A([a],[ρ]), ρ̇=R([a],[ρ]) whose pushforward under τ:(a,ρ)↦{·,·}_{a,ρ} equals Q(P([a],ρ))?
accepted.context_brief: Preservation of Nambu-type brackets on R^3

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Is the class of Poisson brackets {·, ·}a,̺ preserved by any of Kontsevich’s infinitesimal symmetries P˙ = Q(P) ? Specifically, for a given symmetry P˙^ij = Q^ij_Pαβ([a], ̺) of the Poisson bi-vector P = (P^ij), does there exist a well defined evolutionary system a˙ = A([a], [̺]), ̺˙ = R([a], [̺]) such that this vector field in the jet space with fibre variables a, ̺ is pushed forward by the tangent map τ∗ to the symmetry Q(P([a], ̺)), here τ : (a, ̺)(x, y, z) ↦ {·, ·}a,̺|(x,y,z) is the linear differential operator.

accepted.question_text: Which two-parameter Poisson brackets {·,·}_{a,ρ} on R^3 remain invariant under a fixed Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry, meaning Q({·,·}_{a,ρ})≡0 at every point? More generally, which Poisson bi-vectors P satisfy both the Jacobi identity [[P,P]]=0 and the invariance condition Q(P)=0 for a chosen symmetry Q?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Describe those two-parameter Poisson brackets {·, ·}a,̺ on R^3 which stay invariant under a given Kontsevich’s infinitesimal symmetry: Q({·, ·}a,̺) ≡ 0 at all (x, y, z) ∈ R^3. • More generally, describe (classes of) bi-vectors P which are Q-invariant solutions of the Jacobi identity: [[P,P]] = 0 and Q(P) = 0 for a given Q.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds that are simultaneously nonlinear, proper, and nontrivial in Poisson cohomology, meaning they are not of the form [[P,X]] up to terms proportional to [[P,P]]? If no such examples exist, what mechanism forces all currently known universal Poisson cocycles, including those produced from nontrivial graph cocycles by O→r, to become ∂_P-trivial?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Do there exist nonlinear, proper, and still ∂_P-nontrivial infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) ∈ sym([[P,P]] = 0) of Poisson bi-vectors P on finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds M^r_aff ? If the converse it true, what is then the mechanism of ∂_P-triviality of all these Poisson cocycles (in particular, produced by the graph orientation morphism O→r from nontrivial graph cocycles γ ∈ ker d) ?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how many of the countably many universal symmetries obtained by applying O→r to wheel cocycles and their iterated commutators in ker d are globally nonzero sections of Λ^2TM^r_aff rather than vanishing identically?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. For a given affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how many universal symmetries – taken from the countable set O→r(γ ∈ ker d)(P) produced by the graph orientation morphism O→r from the grt-related wheel cocycles and their iterated commutators [14, 29] – do not vanish identically as global sections from Γ(Λ^2TM^r_aff) ?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how large is the family of trivialising vector fields X=X(γ) associated with graph cocycles γ∈ker d? Is the vector space of these vector fields locally complete enough to approximate arbitrary vector fields on the manifold, so that the exponentials of the trivialising fields could effectively imitate a smooth structure on the affine Poisson manifold?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. In the above setting, how ample is the set of trivialising vector fields X = X(γ ∈ ker d) ∈ Γ(TM^r_aff) on a given manifold (M^r_aff,P) with a fixed Poisson structure ? Is the vector space of these fields X locally complete, to be sufficient for the approximation of arbitrary vector fields on M^r_aff ? In brief, are the exponents of the trivialising vector fields X(γ,P) enough to imitate a smooth structure on an affine Poisson manifold ?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a classical model has a Poisson bracket {·,·}_P and an infinitesimal symmetry Q that acts nontrivially on that Poisson structure. After quantisation, must there always be a corresponding well-defined response either on the Hilbert space of states, on the operator algebra of observables, or on both?
accepted.context_brief: Quantised response to a classical symmetry

evidence.quote: Problem 16. For a given infinitesimal symmetry Q ∈ sym{·, ·}_P which acts nontrivially on the Poisson structure {·, ·}_P in a given classical model, so that Q({·, ·}_P) ≢ 0, is there always a well-defined post-quantisation response in either or both the Hilbert space of states or the operator algebra of observables ?

accepted.question_text: How does the graph complex act on the space of deformation-quantisation star-products, especially under gauge transformations ⋆⇄⋆′, when the leading Poisson bi-vector in a Kontsevich star-product ⋆ = × + ħ{·,·}_P + o(ħ) is shifted by a graph-generated symmetry Q(P)=O→r(γ)(P) to P+εQ(P)+o(ε)? Can this action be described explicitly and illustrated by examples?

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Describe and illustrate by examples the action of graph complex on the set of star-products (in particular, in the context of their gauge transformations ⋆ ⇄ ⋆′) whenever the Poisson bi-vector P in the leading deformation term ħP of ⋆ = × + ħ {·, ·}_P + o(ħ) is shifted by a symmetry Q(P) = O→r(γ ∈ ker[•−•, ·])(P) to ħP + εQ(ħP) + o(ε).

accepted.question_text: How do graph-complex symmetries Ṗ=O→r(γ)(P) act on the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson σ-model, whose Feynman path-integral expansion encodes the Kontsevich star-product? In addition, does that σ-model possess symmetries that do not originate from graph cocycles γ in ker d?
accepted.context_brief: Graph symmetries in the Poisson sigma-model

evidence.quote: Problem 18. How does the graph complex act – by the symmetries P˙ = O→r(γ)(P) – on the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson σ-model [13] in which the Feynman path integral expansions of correlation functions [10] encode the Kontsevich star-product ⋆ = × + ħ {·, ·}_P + o(ħ) ? • Does the σ-model in [13] have symmetries not originating from the graphs γ ∈ ker d ?

accepted.question_text: Do universal infinitesimal symmetries Ṗ=Q(P) of classical Poisson structures survive under Batalin–Vilkovisky quantisation, where the classical master equation [[P,P]]=0 is replaced by iħΔP + 1/2[[P,P]] = 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Likewise, do the universal symmetries P˙ = Q(P) ∈ sym([[P,P]] = 0) persist in the course of the Batalin–Vilkovisky quantisation, ([[P,P]] = 0) ⇒ (iħ ΔP + 1/2 [[P,P]] = 0), of Poisson bi-vectors P ?

accepted.question_text: Is there a universal extension of the Kontsevich construction from affine Poisson manifolds to the commutative but non-associative calculus of cyclic words with pair-of-pants multiplication in formal noncommutative or super-geometry, such that it remains well defined for the full family of graph-encoded symmetries Q∈sym([[P,P]]=0) of Poisson structures?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Is there a well-defined – and universal w.r.t. the set Q ∈ sym([[P,P]] = 0) of graph-encoded symmetries of Poisson structures P – generalisation of the Kontsevich construction, originally on affine Poisson manifolds (M^r<∞_aff,P), to the commutative non-associative calculus of cyclic words with their topological pair-of-pants multiplication S^1 × S^1 → S^1 in the Kontsevich formal noncommutative (super)geometry ?
